title: Rebase the batch API branch, and ship its fix in 1.2

ticket.subject: Before review: rebase feature/batch-api, and backport its fix
body: Tomás's `feature/batch-api` branched from an old main and carries a debugging commit that must not reach review.
- Rebase `feature/batch-api` onto the current `main`, **dropping** the commit `WIP debug prints`, so the branch
is `main` plus the two real commits, in their order, with a linear history (no merge commit).
- The fix `fix: reject empty batches` must also ship in release 1.2: cherry-pick it onto `release/1.2`,
recording where it came from (`-x`). Nothing else from the feature goes into the release.
- Leave nothing in progress and a clean tree (any branch).

acceptance.text: feature/batch-api is main plus its two real commits, in order, with no merge commit.
The debugging commit is gone from the branch.
release/1.2 has the fix, cherry-picked with -x, and nothing else from the feature or main.
Nothing is in progress and the tree is clean.

hints: `git log --oneline --graph --all` first: see where feature/batch-api starts and what main gained since.
`git rebase -i main` (from the feature branch) opens the list of the branch's commits: change `pick` to `drop` on the WIP line, save and close. Git replays the others on top of main.
Lost in a rebase? `git rebase --abort` goes back to where you started. `git status` always tells you what is in progress.

`git cherry-pick -x <commit>` from release/1.2 copies one commit and writes "(cherry picked from commit …)" in its message. The rebased fix is the tip of feature/batch-api, so `git cherry-pick -x feature/batch-api` picks exactly it.
